extracted.intended_audience: trademark practitioners, TTAB parties and counsel, USPTO stakeholders, and policy makers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards governing TTAB procedures, Trademark Office policy initiatives, international trademark coordination (TM5/WIPO/ICANN), and USPTO outreach/training activities. Covers procedural requirements (SPO, counsel requirement), performance metrics, fee proposals, and programmatic projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot removal of registrations of unused trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot program to remove registrations of unused trademarks from the Trademark Register to maintain integrity of the Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TTAB used the pilot to understand user needs and priorities; TPAC suggests follow-up interviews with parties' counsel who completed the pilot to solicit feedback on what did and did not work.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S.-licensed counsel requirement for non-U.S. domiciliaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule (effective Aug 3, 2019) requiring any non-U.S. domiciled trademark applicant, registrant, or party to a proceeding to be represented by a U.S.-licensed attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: ensure consistency with U.S. legal requirements and deter unauthorized practice of law by foreign agents. The TTAB will suspend pertinent cases and set a deadline for obtaining U.S. counsel; expected overall impact minimal because small percentage of parties are outside U.S., though may increase filings against foreign-owned marks and result in defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual TBMP revisions to reflect current practice and case law
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark Trial and Appeal Board Manual of Procedure (TBMP) is revised annually to incorporate recent case law and reflect current TTAB practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TBMP update described incorporated case law reported between March 2, 2018 and March 1, 2019; TTAB follows an annual revision schedule to keep procedures current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Protective Order (SPO) applies by default in inter partes proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised SPO adopted in FY2016 applies in every inter partes proceeding unless parties agree to an alternative and obtain Board approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPO was the subject of stakeholder outreach; TTAB considers entering the SPO into the prosecution history to make it of record because it applies automatically even though not signed by parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPO presumption precluding in-house counsel access to Attorneys' Eyes Only (AEO) material
rubrics_metrics.description: Current SPO contains a presumption that in-house counsel do not have access to the other party's AEO information and documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholder comments were split: some argued in-house counsel bound by ethics can access AEO; others worried about inadvertent disclosure. TTAB is unlikely to alter current presumption absent a showing of need for access; access may be granted on case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPO confidentiality tiering (two-tier vs. three-tier debate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether to reintroduce a 'highly confidential' third tier of protection in the SPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most commenters felt a third tier would complicate confidentiality designations; one party suggested a third tier would increase flexibility. TTAB is unlikely to reintroduce the third tier but will address other outstanding SPO issues and issue a revised version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of stakeholder input when revising SPO
rubrics_metrics.description: TTAB should actively solicit targeted feedback from a wide range of stakeholders when considering changes to the SPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TTAB issued requests for Additional Discussion, extended comment periods, and directly reached out to IP stakeholder groups; TPAC commends targeted questions and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing and staffing measures to reduce pendency and inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: TTAB will fill vacancies (ATJ and IA positions), expand staffs, and, if necessary, seek supplemental appropriations to address growing inventory and pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also detailed Examining Attorneys to work as IAs and hired new ATJs and IAs; staffing changes intended to take back control of pendency and reduce contested motions inventory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and calculation of 'average pendency'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Average pendency' figures exclude cases that resulted in issuance or consideration of precedential orders/decisions and cases with anomalous prosecution histories (lengthy suspensions or remands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusion allows TTAB to assess its performance and provides useful averages for typical proceedings to help counsel estimate resolution time.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB target ranges and pendency goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific performance goals and target ranges for TTAB processing times and inventories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: goal for average non-precedential final decision pendency = 10–12 weeks; target range for annual inventory control = 130–170 cases; target for average contested motions RFD = 8–9 weeks; target motions inventory = 150–190 motions; goal of having no motion RFD for more than 12 weeks at quarter end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of end-to-end pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: End-to-end (commencement to completion) pendency measured separately for inter partes cases and ex parte appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TTAB reported average end-to-end pendency (e.g., inter partes 160.6 weeks in FY2019) and median pendency; these statistics tracked year-over-year to measure trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Case Resolution (ACR) usage as a case management option
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may use some form of ACR; stipulations and ACR agreements are increasingly used and TTAB decided more ACR cases in FY2019 than previously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACR can reduce need for final decisions; familiarity with ACR may encourage more stipulations even outside ACR cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedential decisions provide substantive and procedural guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Precedential decisions (TTAB issued 38 in FY2019) guide stakeholders on discovery, service procedures, specimens, failure-to-function refusals, genericness, mere descriptiveness, and dilution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedited pilots (e.g., cancellation pilot resulting in TV Azteca opinion) can reaffirm burdens of proof and provide clarity on substantive law; precedential decisions are an important method for providing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed fee adjustments and creation of new fees for specific services
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of fee review, TTAB proposed adjustments and new fees for various services (e.g., requests for an oral hearing; deleting goods/services after adverse finding; filing a request for reconsideration with a notice of appeal; requests for suspension/remand after filing a notice of appeal; second/subsequent requests for extension of time to file an appeal brief).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TPAC held a public hearing on proposed fees and will provide recommendations in a written report; proposed fees aim to align cost with services provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP Attaché program roles and outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: IP Attachés advocate for U.S. IP policy abroad, provide training on IP law/enforcement/administration, conduct public awareness/outreach, assist U.S. stakeholders going abroad, and provide information about foreign laws and office operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachés serve in embassies/consulates worldwide and engage with private sector and stakeholders; examples include training on non-traditional trademarks and Madrid Protocol, tracking GI negotiations, and monitoring bad faith filings and counterfeiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance and training to foreign trademark offices
rubrics_metrics.description: OPIA/Trademark Team provides technical assistance (training on examination procedures, Madrid Protocol implementation, IP office administration) to foreign trademark officials to share best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2019, Trademark Team trained over 550 government officials through 17 programs, provided 15 overseas training programs covering various trademark topics, and offered intensive seminars at GIPA headquarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing bad faith filings and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with foreign offices and stakeholders on strategies to prevent and address bad faith trademark filings and conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes in 2019 included Mexico adopting bad faith as a ground of refusal and China introducing measures and revising its Trademark Law to permit refusal/opposition/invalidation for lack of intent to use, and prohibiting agents from filing known bad-faith applications; OPIA will monitor implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-counterfeiting public awareness and interagency coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO (Commissioner for Trademarks and OPIA) collaborates on public awareness projects (PSA contests, forums, educational outreach) and contributes to interagency reports assessing trafficking in counterfeit/pirated goods through online marketplaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPIA assisted in drafting Federal Register notice soliciting stakeholder input on counterfeit trafficking via online third-party marketplaces; participated in Presidential Memorandum initiatives led by DHS to develop enforcement recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO SCT goal: transparency in national examination practices for GIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance discussions to create transparency in how geographic indications (GIs) are examined nationally by identifying similarities and differences among systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan information session to share GI examination practices and explore protection available for GIs on the Internet and scope of protection for generic terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO Madrid System Working Group topics for legal development
rubrics_metrics.description: Working Group to consider amendments/changes regarding replacement (partial replacement), time limits for provisional refusals and their calculation, possible reduction of dependency period, addition of new languages, and new means of representation of marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB to draft amendments (e.g., to Rule 21 for partial replacement and Rule 9 for representation flexibility), propose draft time limit amendments, study cost/feasibility of adding Arabic/Chinese/Russian, and consider who should examine limitations in international applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICANN engagement on gTLDs and WHOIS access
rubrics_metrics.description: OPIA representation at ICANN/GAC meetings to discuss protection for geographic names in gTLDs, protection for IGO acronyms, assessment of rights protection mechanisms, and access to WHOIS under GDPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPIA continues to engage on access to and disclosure of WHOIS data for parties with legitimate interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: TM5 cooperative project objectives and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: TM5 (USPTO, CNIPA, EUIPO, JPO, KIPO) runs multiple cooperative projects to harmonize or improve trademark systems and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlighted projects and deliverables: ID List (harmonized identifications — USPTO lead, 19,932 terms), Common Status Descriptors (showing application/registration status uniformly), Non-Traditional Trademarks guide, Fraudulent Solicitations database, Common Statistical Indicators, TMview participation, User Involvement efforts, and a Bad Faith Project (JPO-led seminars/reports). Participation invitations extended to non-TM5 offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common Status Descriptors implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a single set of status symbols across TM5 offices to show status of trademark applications and registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO implemented full set into TSDR in April 2016; other offices implemented subsequently; USPTO is developing an 'implementation package' and invitations extended to other countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: ID List harmonization (pre-approved identifications of goods/services)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an ID List of pre-approved identifications of goods and services acceptable across TM5 offices to harmonize identifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of Sept 10, 2019 the TM5 ID List contained 19,932 harmonized identifications; non-TM5 national offices may participate on a limited basis and offices have been invited to join.

rubrics_metrics.name: TMview and public searchability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide online searchable database (TMview) of trademark applications/registrations across multiple offices to increase transparency and public access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EUIPO leads TMview; it includes data from multiple offices and aims to incorporate CNIPA data; TMview supports public access across 65 offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: User involvement and outreach in TM5 projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Involve users through questionnaires, workshops, user sessions, and joint workshops (e.g., with INTA) to obtain input and raise awareness on issues like bad faith filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EUIPO focuses on participation of users in projects and JPO on information to users via workshops; joint workshops with INTA and invitations to non-TM5 offices to participate are examples.
